patient.chief_complaint: Husband called 911 - wife having focal motor seizure right arm that spread, now continuous 18 minutes
patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. Thompson is a 68-year-old woman with right frontal glioblastoma on bevacizumab and dexamethasone who is brought by ambulance after her husband called 911 when she developed a focal motor seizure involving the right arm that progressively spread and secondarily generalized to bilateral tonic-clonic activity. The seizure has been continuous for approximately 18 minutes. She had her most recent bevacizumab infusion 5 days ago. Her husband notes she has been increasingly fatigued and had worsening headaches over the past 10 days, which she attributed to the GBM. She missed her morning levetiracetam dose today due to nausea from the bevacizumab. Her dexamethasone was recently tapered from 8 mg/day to 4 mg/day over the past 2 weeks on oncology's instruction. The combination of: (1) subtherapeutic levetiracetam from missed dose, (2) steroid taper leading to rebound cerebral edema, and (3) possible tumor progression all potentially precipitated this SE. She has progressive disease that has been growing despite bevacizumab. The citalopram lowers seizure threshold and may prolong QTc. Right frontal tumor location predicts right-sided focal seizures with contralateral (left) arm involvement - note she is right-handed so this would affect her dominant hand.
